extraction.name: Video-MME
extraction.description: A comprehensive multimodal evaluation benchmark for video analysis by MLLMs, consisting of 900 videos and 2,700 manually annotated multiple-choice questions across diverse domains, durations, and modalities including subtitles and audio.
extraction.creator: Chaoyou Fu, Yuhan Dai, Yongdong Luo, Lei Li, Shuhuai Ren, Renrui Zhang, Zihan Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Yunhang Shen, Mengdan Zhang, Peixian Chen, Yanwei Li, Shaohui Lin, Sirui Zhao, Ke Li, Tong Xu, Xiawu Zheng, Enhong Chen, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Xing Sun
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed in three steps: collecting raw videos from YouTube across a predefined domain hierarchy, manually annotating each video with multiple-choice QA pairs by recruited annotators, and conducting manual quality review plus filtering of text-answerable questions using Gemini 1.5 Pro.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consisted of YouTube videos from 6 domains and 30 fine-grained categories, along with corresponding subtitles when available and audio files.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Manual expert annotation of multiple-choice QA pairs for each video, followed by independent manual review and machine-assisted filtering for text-only answerability. Annotators with strong English proficiency and vision-language research experience watched the full video and created three questions with four options each; a different annotator then checked clarity, answerability, option consistency, and correctness, and questions answerable without the video were revised.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality validation included independent second-annotator review and filtering with Gemini 1.5 Pro to remove questions answerable from text alone; the paper reports Gemini 1.5 Pro achieved less than 15% accuracy in the text-only setup.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 QA pairs per video, plus 1 additional review by a different annotator for each QA pair.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators had strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini 1.5 Pro was used to test text-only questions and filter out QA pairs that could be answered without viewing the video.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes a long-tailed distribution in datasets for complex temporal reasoning in long videos, which creates acquisition challenges and suggests uneven data coverage.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Current video datasets and models are limited in handling long videos and complex temporal reasoning. Model performance declines as video duration increases, restricted input frames create an information bottleneck, and existing instruction-tuning datasets are dominated by short-input datasets with limited availability of long-video temporal reasoning data.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The discussed datasets are intended for instruction-tuning and training supervision to improve temporal reasoning and robust temporal understanding in video MLLMs.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Videos were collected to achieve relatively balanced duration distribution across short, medium, and long categories, and QA pairs answerable from text-only questions were filtered out and returned for revision.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A rigorous manual quality review was performed on QA pairs to verify clear and precise language, answerability, logical consistency of options, and correctness of the designated answer; text-only-answerable questions were identified using Gemini 1.5 Pro and excluded/revised.

name.evidence: In this paper, we introduce Video-MME, the first-ever full-spectrum, Multi-Modal Evaluation benchmark of MLLMs in Video analysis.

description.evidence: we introduce Video-MME, the first-ever full-spectrum, Multi-Modal Evaluation benchmark of MLLMs in Video analysis... we meticulously curate a dataset of 900 videos across various scenarios, and annotate a set of 2,700 high-quality multiple-choice questions

rai:dataCollection.evidence: “The construction of the Video-MME dataset involves three main steps: video collection, question-answer annotation, and quality review.”

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: “we first establish a domain hierarchy for sourcing raw videos from YouTube”

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: “we first establish a domain hierarchy for sourcing raw videos from YouTube... yielding a total of 30 finely-grained video categories... we also obtain corresponding meta-information such as subtitles (if provided) and audios”

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: “we employ a multiple-choice QA format ... recruit annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language leaming. Specifically, each annotator is tasked with thoroughly viewing the entire video, then iteratively creating three relevant questions, each accompanied by four candidate options” and “each QA pair undergoes examination by a different annotator to verify that (i) the language expression is clear and precise; (ii) the question is answerable with logically consistent candidate options, and the designated correct answer is appropriate.”

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: “we provide the text-only questions to Gemini 1.5 Pro and filter out QA pairs that can be answered solely based on the textual questions” and “Statistical analysis shows that Gemini 1.5 Pro achieves less than 15% accuracy in the text-only setup”

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: “annotate a set of 2,700 high-quality multiple-choice questions (3 per video)” and “each QA pair undergoes examination by a different annotator”

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: “recruit annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language leaming”

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: “we provide the text-only questions to Gemini 1.5 Pro and filter out QA pairs that can be answered solely based on the textual questions”

rai:dataBiases.evidence: The long-tailed distribution of this data poses challenges for acquisition.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: One of the significant challenges identified in our evaluation is the decline in performance as video duration increases. For open-source models, the restricted input frames can become an information bottleneck for understanding the full content of long videos... Although there have been efforts to construct high-quality datasets involving complex temporal reasoning in long videos [26, 45], the availability of such datasets remains limited compared to those for text [42, 46] and image [30, 65].

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: Our evaluation emphasizes the need for instruction-tuning datasets focused on temporal reasoning... Developing these datasets will enable better use of architectural innovations, providing MLLMs with sufficient training supervision for robust temporal understanding in videos.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: “For each category, we collect videos with varying duration lengths, including short (<2 minutes), medium (4-15 minutes), and long videos (30-60 minutes).” and “the resulting dataset consists of 900 videos... representing a range of domains with a relatively balanced distribution of video durations” and “we provide the text-only questions to Gemini 1.5 Pro and filter out QA pairs that can be answered solely based on the textual questions... Questions that do not meet this criterion are returned to the original annotator for revision.”

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: “To guarantee the quality of our dataset, we conduct a rigorous manual review process. First, each QA pair undergoes examination by a different annotator to verify that (i) the language expression is clear and precise; (ii) the question is answerable with logically consistent candidate options, and the designated correct answer is appropriate.” and “we provide the text-only questions to Gemini 1.5 Pro and filter out QA pairs that can be answered solely based on the textual questions.”
